subject: Discovery Recap: FinHealth Private/VPC Requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Sullivan <anna.sullivan@finhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery Recap: FinHealth Private/VPC Requirements

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Below is a short recap from our discovery so everyone has the same set of notes and next steps. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

Summary of pain points / constraints
- Regulated workloads: PHI and financial PII; strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Customer-managed keys required (KMS/HSM) — you need HSM-backed key control and no keys stored in a shared service.
- Network constraints: no direct outbound internet from compute nodes; updates must go through a controlled jumpbox/proxy.
- Air-gap considerations: ability to run in an offline environment and to apply vetted updates through an orchestrated package process.
- Limited egress: model telemetry and logs must stay in your VPC or be routed to approved endpoints only.

Current stack (as stated)
- Private cloud (KVM-based), orchestration via upstream Kubernetes (internal distro)
- Internal model store for some in-house models; evaluating Redwood for inference serving on dedicated GPU hosts
- On-prem SIEM and centralized KMS (HashiCorp Vault with HSM plugin)

Success criteria for a pilot
- Deployment inside FinHealth VPC with no data egress outside approved endpoints
- Use of customer-managed keys (HSM) for encryption at rest and for token encryption if possible
- Audit logs integrated into your SIEM; retention policy support for 7+ years
- Validated update process that meets your change-control rules (air-gap-compatible)

Agreed next steps
1) Vivek (SE) to share a Private Deployment checklist and minimal network/topology requirements (attached). [Attachment: redwood-private-deployment-checklist.pdf]
2) Anna to share network topology and the security requirements spreadsheet (you mentioned infra team would provide).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) with FinHealth infra + security, Vivek, and Neha.
4) Redwood to provide SOC 2 artifacts and an example KMS integration guide for HSM-backed Vault setups.

Proposed times for deep-dive: Tue 10th (10–11am PT) or Wed 11th (1–2pm PT). Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: FinHealth Private/VPC Requirements

Anna / Marissa — thanks for the summary, Marissa. A few technical clarifications from my side: 

- For HSM-backed keys: can you confirm your Vault setup exposes an external PKCS#11 interface or do you rely on a Cloud HSM appliance? That will change our connector approach.
- For the air-gap/update flow: do you have an existing process for importing signed software bundles? If yes, can you share the acceptance checklist or signing process?
- Network: we’ll need the CIDR ranges for any jumpboxes/proxies and the egress allowlist for package update endpoints. We can scope an isolated outbound proxy pattern so the inference hosts do not have general internet access.

Attaching the checklist Marissa referenced — it includes the minimal ports, ranges, and service-to-service requirements. Happy to go through this in the deep-dive and mark items as "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" for the pilot.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — this looks correct. A few clarifications / attachments from our side: 

- We confirm HSM-backed Vault via on-prem HSM appliance (Thales); Vault is accessed via PKCS#11.
- Update process: we currently sign packages internally. We require a signed manifest and checksum verification before any install.
- Jumpbox: infra will provide the jumpbox IPs and proxy hostnames — attaching a topology snapshot now.
- Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and data deletion proof (for eDiscovery). Please include example logs/audit formats you export.

Attachments: network-topology-snapshot.png, finhealth-security-reqs.xlsx
